sections.title: Accommodation Inquiry
sections.context: A student is inquiring about housing options at the university accommodation office.

transcript.speaker: Mrs. Gable
transcript.text: Good morning! University Accommodation Office, Mrs. Gable speaking. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: Hi, good morning. My name is Alex Thorne, and I'm a second-year student. I’m looking for a place to stay for the upcoming autumn semester.

transcript.speaker: Mrs. Gable
transcript.text: Hello, Alex. Let me just open the registration form here. Could you spell your last name for me?

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: Yes, it’s Thorne. T-H-O-R-N-E.

transcript.speaker: Mrs. Gable
transcript.text: Got it. And I’ll need your student identification number to access your records.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: Sure. It is 8-8-4-1... oh, wait, sorry. I’m looking at my old library card by mistake. My actual student ID is 8-8-5-1.

transcript.speaker: Mrs. Gable
transcript.text: 8-8-5-1. Thank you. Now, do you have a preference for which part of the city you'd like to live in?

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: Well, most of my classes are on the South Campus, so I initially thought about North Hill, but a friend told me it’s way too noisy there at night. I think I’d prefer the West Village area. It’s a bit quieter.

transcript.speaker: Mrs. Gable
transcript.text: West Village is a very popular choice. Now, regarding your budget, what is the maximum monthly rent you are willing to pay?

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: I was hoping for something around four hundred pounds, but I know prices have gone up. I can go up to five hundred, but absolutely no more than five hundred and fifty pounds per month, including utilities.

transcript.speaker: Mrs. Gable
transcript.text: I'll put down five hundred and fifty as the upper limit. And what type of room are you looking for? We have shared rooms, singles, and studios.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: I really need my own space to study, so a single is what I'm after. Preferably an ensuite if possible, so I don't have to share a bathroom.

transcript.speaker: Mrs. Gable
transcript.text: Understood. A single ensuite. And when were you planning to move in?

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: The semester starts on the 18th, so I was hoping to get settled on the 12th of September.

transcript.speaker: Mrs. Gable
transcript.text: Let me check the maintenance schedule... unfortunately, the cleaning crews won't be finished with the West Village blocks until the 14th. The earliest move-in date we can offer is the 15th of September.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: The 15th? That’s only three days before classes start, but I guess it will have to do. Please mark that down.

transcript.speaker: Mrs. Gable
transcript.text: Done. Now, let me tell you a bit about the facilities in that area. It’s very convenient. The main library is only about a 10 minutes walk away, which is great for late-night study sessions.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: That sounds perfect. What about laundry? I heard some blocks don't have machines.

transcript.speaker: Mrs. Gable
transcript.text: All our West Village buildings have a dedicated laundry room on the ground floor. You just use a mobile app to pay for the cycles. Also, there's a small gym on-site, though you have to pay a separate membership fee for that.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: I'm not much of a gym person, so that's fine. Are there any extra fees I should know about before I sign?

transcript.speaker: Mrs. Gable
transcript.text: There is a standard security deposit, and we also require a key deposit of thirty pounds. You get that back when you return the keys at the end of the year.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: Thirty pounds is reasonable. And is the internet connection included in the rent?

transcript.speaker: Mrs. Gable
transcript.text: Yes, high-speed internet is included in the price. You won't have to pay anything extra for Wi-Fi in your room or the common areas.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: That’s great news. Thank you so much for your help, Mrs. Gable.

transcript.speaker: Mrs. Gable
transcript.text: You're very welcome, Alex. I'll send you the official offer via email by this afternoon.
